content: I'll start by reading the test image to analyze the visual symptoms.

The test image shows dense white cottony mycelium with small round yellowish sclerotia at what appears to be the stem/crown area. This is characteristic of Southern Blight or Sclerotinia. Let me view a reference image for Southern Blight to confirm.

The reference dataset is not available on the local filesystem. I'll rely on my analysis of the test image alone.

**Test Image Analysis:**
- **Affected part:** Stem/crown (base of plant)
- **Visual features:**
  - Dense, white fluffy/cottony mycelium covering the entire crown/stem area
  - Numerous small, round, yellowish/tan sclerotia (roughly mustard-seed sized, ~1-2mm) embedded throughout the mycelium
  - Brown necrotic stem tissue visible beneath the mycelium
  - The mycelium radiates outward from the infected stem center

**Reasoning:**
The combination of dense white cottony mycelium + small round mustard-seed-sized sclerotia at the stem base is the textbook hallmark of **Southern Blight** (*Sclerotium rolfsii*). The sclerotia are clearly small and round (not large/irregular/black as in Sclerotinia), ruling out Sclerotinia Timber Rot. No bacterial wilt candidates would show this fungal growth. Gray Mold produces grayish sporulation without these characteristic sclerotia. The image Bugwood ID 1578614 is also associated with S. rolfsii in plant pathology databases.
